text:
Alice: heads up — after the v3.8.2 canary rollout (runtime pool C), we’re seeing a spike in streaming client disconnects and paging errors. getting paged now.
DeployBot: @Alice detected deploy v3.8.2 -> canary group: runtime-pool-c at 2278904300. health_check failures 11% over 5m.
Bob: oncall here, joining. what’s the exact symptom? are clients failing to re-open streams or just slow responses?
Alice: most failures are handshake/frame decode errors right after connection; not pure latency. customers with long-running streams drop with error: `ERR_STREAM_FRAME_UNEXPECTED` in server logs.
Carol: pulling logs. snippets: ```
[2278904312] conn=abcd1234 ERR_STREAM_FRAME_UNEXPECTED: frame_type=0x7f seq=342
[2278904312] stack: serve->decode_frame->panic
```
Bob: that looks like a protocol mismatch. did the client sdk just bump framing?
Dave: Support: escalation from customer X reporting 30% of their sessions ended in last 10 minutes. They see reconnect storms.
Alice: this canary was supposed to be a safe runtime change (kernel selection tweak). no SDK changes in the release. but code diff includes an opt-in streaming framing refactor (guarded behind flag).
Carol: grep shows the runtime reads `STREAM_FRAME_VERSION` from env but default fallback changed — older clients expect v1 but canary is advertising v2 in handshake.
Oncall-ML: marking P1 and paging Eng-SRE. I’m taking incident lead until handoff.
Bob: immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle feature flag to advertise v1, 2) pause canary rollout (kill-switch), 3) rollback canary. Which is fastest?
Alice: kill-switch exists: `ff.runtime.streaming_v2` — can flip in prod config service within 30s. rolling that first to verify.
DeployBot: feature-flag toggle requested by @Alice. executing...
DeployBot: feature-flag `runtime.streaming_v2` -> OFF (scope: runtime-pool-c) at 2278904430.
Carol: monitoring metrics. connection error rate dropping on pool-c from 9% -> 2% within 60s. looks promising.
Dave: customer X reports degraded but stable sessions. they’ll keep monitoring.
Bob: good call. do we need full rollback or just keep flag off until we patch advertising behavior?
Alice: we should pause further rollouts to other pools. I’m pausing the release pipeline.
Alice: `ci/release` pipeline -> PAUSED by @Alice at 2278904475.
Oncall-ML: handoff scheduled for 1 hour. Postmortem owner? Carol can you take root cause and fix plan?
Carol: I’ll own postmortem. immediate next steps: reproduce locally with v2 advertisement, add strict version negotiation fallback (server shouldn't advertise v2 to v1-only clients), add integration test on handshake matrix.
Bob: SRE actions: keep flag off globally for all runtime pools until patch verified. also roll forward canary to include negotiation fix or rollback to previous runtime binary?
Alice: negotiation fix faster than full rollback. we can build patch -> canary in pool-c with flag off, run matrix tests, then turn flag on again.
DeployBot: pipeline resumed? No — pipeline remains paused.
Dave: Communications: Sending an update to affected customers: short blurb that we hit a canary handshake mismatch, feature-flag kill used, sessions restored, follow-up with timeline and RCA to come.
Carol: creating PR with fix: `server/streaming: add handshake_negotiation_v1_fallback` — will run canary images in staging then pool-c.
Bob: leaving a note for after-hours oncall: if error rate creeps >5% revert flag and contact Carol.
Oncall-ML: acknowledged. handing off to night shift @Bob at 2278905100. I’ll post final summary when we close.
Alice: thanks all. quick retrospective: accidental default advertisement flip should have been covered by e2e handshake tests. add to action items.
DeployBot: incident created: INC-2026-0315-001. severity: P1.
Oncall-ML: final status: Mitigated — feature flag kill-switch executed, customer impact reduced to degraded for ~45m, no data loss. owners: Carol (RCA + fix), Bob (sre follow-up), Dave (customer comm). next update planned in 24h.
Carol: opening postmortem draft now and attaching logs/traces.
Dave: sent update to customer X and a Slack thread to account teams.
Bob: closing active pager. leaving notes in runbook to verify handshake matrix on future runtime changes.
Alice: appreciate the quick response.
notes: incident-bot created INC-2026-0315-001; feature-flag kill-switch used; handoff to night oncall at 2278905100
